{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693639987,"sessionID":"ses_e23eec6d4ffebFQbW2CiqdwWBL","part":{"id":"prt_1dc13a808001LV06V3FVRl1e5N","messageID":"msg_1dc1389c3001ICs03NUK0JE4EL","sessionID":"ses_e23eec6d4ffebFQbW2CiqdwWBL","type":"text","text":"The shift is over. All four customer-facing services were at 0% errors from minute 61 to minute 63, and again from minute 91 to the end of the shift at minute 120. No throttles are on.\n\nI found four separate causes and fixed each one. After every fix, the service stayed overloaded because callers kept retrying failed requests, so each fix also needed a temporary scale-up.\n\n1. **flags-svc memory leak** (mobile-api and admin-portal, ~97% errors at the page): deploy v34 was leaking memory. I rolled it back at minute 7 and scaled from 3 to 6 replicas to clear the retries. It recovered by minute 29, and I set it back to 3.\n2. **sms-svc schema change** (web-storefront and partner-api, ~4% errors at the page): deploy v24 changed the wire schema from v2 to v3, which bundles-svc couldn't decode. I rolled it back at minute 22. The rollback briefly pushed web-storefront to 55% errors because of the retries. I scaled to 24 replicas, errors hit 0% by minute 37, and I brought it down to 10.\n3. **inventory-svc rate-limiter bug** (mobile-api and admin-portal stayed around 75% errors): deploy v163 divided the rate limiter's refill rate by 1000. I rolled it back at minute 48 and scaled to 24. It recovered by minute 61 and is now at 10.\n4. **events-queue TLS change** (a new fault at minute 63: mobile-api, partner-api and admin-portal at 92–99% errors): config cfg-47 raised the minimum TLS version from 1.2 to 1.3, so callers' connections failed. I reverted it at minute 83 and scaled to 24. It recovered by minute 91 and is now at 10.\n\nI left several changes alone because they didn't cause anything: the bundles-svc config cfg-49, the sms-svc config cfg-61, the inventory-svc config cfg-31 and the events-queue deploy v102. The images-svc CPU alert also never caused customer errors, and I didn't touch it.\n\nThree services finished above their normal replica counts, which costs $3 per extra replica per minute:\n- **sms-svc:** 10 instead of 8.\n- **inventory-svc:** 10 instead of 8.\n- **events-queue:** 10 instead of 8.\n\nI kept the extra replicas on purpose. inventory-svc and events-queue would run at about 80% CPU on their normal counts, which leaves too little room before the next retry storm. The same reasoning applies to sms-svc, though I didn't measure its exact load.\n\nThe biggest cost was web-storefront ($22,900/min). It ran at about 4% errors until minute 22, then at roughly 50–55% while the sms-svc rollback ran and retries cleared, until minute 37.","time":{"start":1794693638152,"end":1794693639980}}}
